about.text: An Egyptian cheese made by fermenting salted soft cheese, traditionally Areesh, for a year or more in an earthenware jar under a pickle of buttermilk, sour milk, whey and peppers. It turns yellowish-brown, sharp and pungent. The jar can be topped up with fresh cheese for years.

links.name: Wikipedia (citing Robinson & Tamime, Feta and Related Cheeses, 1991)

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Salted fresh cheese is packed into a jar and covered with a sour pickle; fermentation runs for a year or more, giving a very salty, sharp, soft cheese.

steps.note: Sealed in an earthenware jar under a pickle of buttermilk, sour skimmed milk, whey and red and green peppers, with a little older mish as starter.

processing.text: The jar is topped up as cheese is taken out and fresh added, so there is no fixed age.
